Hi Samir / Contracts team —

Attached is our proposed Exhibit B (service schedule) and the updated order form that reflects the capacity uplift you requested in last week’s call. Key points summarized below so it’s easy to review:

- Term: proposing a 24-month renewal term to lock in the uplift pricing and avoid large step changes at next renewal.
- Capacity uplift: +40% baseline GPU hours (see Capacity-Uplift-OrderForm.xlsx). Pricing tiers updated to reflect volume discount starting at 30% uplift.
- Pricing: per-token rates adjusted per the attached schedule. We included a blended rate for the first 3 months to smooth proration.
- SLA: preserving published latency SLOs; we added an addendum for priority capacity during scheduled releases.
- Data residency: Exhibit B includes region = us (multi-region fallback to us-west).

Can you please:
1) Review Exhibit-B-draft-v2.docx and send redlines (tracked changes or PDF with comments) by EOD Friday 4/16 so Legal has time to reconcile;
2) Confirm whether Helio requires a shorter term (12 months) or has a target go-live date that affects proration;
3) Flag any procurement/corporate approvals needed on your side (PO, SOW format, etc.).

We’re happy to set a 30-min sync with Legal if helpful — otherwise we’ll incorporate your redlines and route a consolidated counter to Contracts.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Aditya Rao

Aditya —

Thanks for the draft. I’m attaching a PDF with our redlines (HelioHealth-redlines-20270416.pdf). High level items from Legal/Procurement:

1) Term: Helio prefers 12 months for this renewal window given our internal budgeting cadence. We are open to a multi-year discussion but need the accounting to reflect 12 months now.
2) Pricing uplift: we cannot accept a 24-month locked blended rate. Our ask: preserve current base rate and apply uplift pricing only for incremental capacity (i.e., incremental tokens at the new tier).
3) SLA / Credits: we need explicit uptime / credit language for dedicated capacity windows — currently the draft references SLOs but not credits.
4) Data residency: must ensure processing of PII stays in us-east for certain workloads. Please confirm that Exhibit B can specify region per workload or provide an exceptions workflow.
5) Procurement format: Contracts prefers a PO-first flow; we will share a PO once terms are agreed.

We attached comments inline and added a short cover memo with suggested alternate clause language. If Redwood can meet us on term = 12 months and the incremental-price treatment for uplift, we can expedite approval on our side.

Samir
Head of Platform Partnerships | HelioHealth

Marissa / Laura — forwarding Samir’s redlines from Helio (attached). Quick thoughts:

On Sat, Apr 16, 2027 at 10:22 AM Samir Patel <samir.patel@heliohealth.com> wrote:
> (see attached HelioHealth-redlines-20270416.pdf)
>
> High level asks: term = 12 months, incremental pricing for uplift, explicit credit language for SLA, data residency to us-east for PII.

My read / proposed response:
- Term: we can offer 12 months but the discount they asked for (tier change at 30% uplift) was premised on a 24-month commitment. If we drop to 12 months we should retain a smaller uplift discount (e.g., 20% at 30% uplift) or offer a one-time onboarding credit to bridge the economics.
- Incremental pricing: this is reasonable; we can model incremental token pricing in the order form but need to ensure the runtime capacity reservation economics still hold (we incur infra reservation costs). Suggest adding a small fixed reservation fee on the order form to cover base capacity provisioning.
- SLA credits: legal should weigh in on the exact credit formula but we should be prepared to include a tiered credit schedule for priority capacity windows.
- Data residency: Laura — is the per-workload residency exception doable? If not, we need to propose a region-specific appendix and an exceptions process (tech + legal sign-off).

Propose a 30-min call Monday with Procurement + Legal + Samir to get to a single redline set. If Legal prefers, we can pre-populate counter language and route via DocuSign once agreed.

I’ll hold off replying to Samir until I get your guidance.

Aditya

Subject: Re: Exhibit B draft + capacity uplift proposal for renewal — Redwood position

Samir / Contracts team —

Thanks for the detailed redlines and the cover memo. We reviewed internally (Product, Sales, Legal) and can respond as follows:

1) Term: We will accept a 12-month term for this renewal on the condition that the uplift pricing is treated as incremental (as you requested) and that we preserve a modest reservation fee to secure capacity for peak windows. This reservation fee will be reflected line-item on the order form and is refundable if Helio converts to a 24-month commitment during the term.

2) Pricing treatment (incremental): We will model incremental token pricing on the attached Capacity-Uplift-OrderForm.xlsx and provide a worked example for the initial three billing cycles to show blended vs incremental comparisons.

3) SLA / Credits: We can incorporate explicit credit language. Legal proposes a tiered credit table tied to latency and availability thresholds for dedicated capacity windows. Please point us to any specific numbers Helio expects and we’ll try to align.

4) Data residency: We cannot guarantee per-workload dynamic residency without an exceptions workflow. Proposed path: Exhibit B will specify region = us-east for PII workloads and us-west for non-PII by default; exceptions require a signed variance request with a defined technical implementation lead and an agreed timeline. We will include an exceptions appendix to capture this workflow.

Next steps:
- Aditya will incorporate the incremental pricing language and reservation fee into the order form and provide a redline counter to your PDF by EOD Monday 4/19.
- If Helio is agreeable, we will prepare a single consolidated counter with DocuSign-ready exhibits and share the link for signature.
- We are available for a 30-min alignment call Monday afternoon; suggest 2pm PT.

If that approach works for you, we’ll proceed and target an executed amendment by end of month.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal | Redwood Inference
